title: The thirty at the Harmandir
hookLine: tradition says thirty Sikhs with Baba Gurbakhsh Singh stayed to defend the Harmandir

cards: Word reaches Amritsar that the invader is coming back. The main bands of the Khalsa are far off. The Harmandir still bears the scars of the last time.
Anyone with sense would pack up and go, and people do go, down the roads out of the city. But tradition says a small group stays, around an older Sikh named Baba Gurbakhsh Singh. Not an army.
A handful. Tradition gives the number as thirty.

teach.b: Start with what they were not doing. They were not expecting to win. Nobody in this story imagines thirty people stopping an army.
That's what makes it worth telling.

teach.h: KEEPING THE PLACE FROM BEING LEFT EMPTY.
teach.b: Then, what they were doing: keeping a place from being left empty. The Harmandir was where the Guru's word was sung, day after day.
Tradition says that before the army arrived, the thirty prepared the way Sikhs prepare for anything serious: they bathed, they prayed, they listened to the Guru's word.
When the army came, they went out to meet it rather than wait behind the walls. And they died, every one, tradition says, with Baba Gurbakhsh Singh. Then, how Sikhs keep it.

teach.h: A MARTYRS' BUNGA NEAR THE AKAL TAKHT.
teach.b: Near the Akal Takht in Amritsar there's a place that bears his name, a shaheedi bunga, a martyrs' tower, remembering him and the others. People praying at the Harmandir today walk past the spot that remembers the thirty.
And last, the part for an ordinary day. Not everyone is asked to be brave in a big way.
Plenty of duties are small and unwatched: the one who stays to lock up, the one who keeps showing up when everyone else drifts off, the one who stays on the phone.
The thirty are remembered for staying where they were needed when there was no hope of a reward.

how: Sikhs remember Baba Gurbakhsh Singh and his companions among the martyrs, and at the Harmandir Sahib complex a place near the Akal Takht bears his name.

games.why: tradition says the thirty prepared, went out to meet the army, and died. Sikhs remember them among the martyrs.

practice: Sit up a little, as if you're on watch, and bring to mind one thing that's yours to keep: a promise, a plant someone asked you to water, a person who counts on your call.
Picture yourself staying with it today, even when drifting off would be easy, and feel your feet on the floor while you hold it. If you pray, say Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Shaheedi bunga, a martyrs' tower near the Akal Takht remembering Baba Gurbakhsh Singh and the thirty who stayed to defend the Harmandir.

orig.note: Gurmukhi for shaheed, a martyr, the word Sikhs use for Baba Gurbakhsh Singh and the thirty.
